messages:
ben_acme: Hey team — our rerank traffic started getting 429s this morning. We're only sending ~10 req/s but it's failing with RerankRateLimitExceeded. Dashboard shows quota still available. Can someone check? :frowning:

alice_support: Sorry to hear that, Ben. Can you paste a sample request + full response headers (especially X-RateLimit, Retry-After)? Also how many candidates per request and whether you batch them?

ben_acme: Here you go — stripped auth token. We're calling POST /v1/rerank with ~50 candidates most requests. Example body:```json
{
  "query": "find the best intro line for cold outreach",
  "candidates": ["Option A", "Option B", "Option C", /* ~50 total */],
  "max_results": 5
}
```Response headers:```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-RateLimit-Limit: 120
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1802604500
Retry-After: 30
Request-Id: r-9a3bf

Body:
{ "error": { "type": "rate_limit", "message": "RerankRateLimitExceeded", "meta": { "units_consumed": 360 } } }
```Weird part: dashboard says we've used 20/120 units this window. So headers + dashboard mismatch.

alice_support: Thanks — that mismatch is exactly what I'm worried about. Looping in eng-runtime and eng-sre. carol_runtime and dave_sre FYI — customer sees 429s from rerank with units_consumed=360 in body but account dashboard shows low usage. They send ~10 rps with ~50 candidates each.

carol_runtime: looking. Quick Q: do you know if candidates are counted as individual "units" or if the rerank endpoint charges per candidate *and* per-token? Historically rerank counted 1 unit per candidate up to a cap.

dave_sre: also want logs from the gateway for that Request-Id. alice, can you grab `edge-proxy` access logs for r-9a3bf and the internal rate limiter traces?

alice_support: attaching logs (redacted):```text
[edge-proxy] r-9a3bf - 1802604321 - POST /v1/rerank - client=acme - candidates=50 - status=429 - rl_key=rerank_global - units_reported=360
[quota-service] account=acme - window_start=1802604000 - total_used=20 - per_endpoint_rerank=0
[rl-policy] rl_key=rerank_global - limit=120/min - burst=240 - observed_rate=11 rps
```So the proxy reports units_reported=360 while quota-service has total_used=20.

carol_runtime: that smells like a mismatch between the proxy-side accounting and the central quota service. Recent change in PR #4237 changed unit calculation for rerank to multiply by `candidates.length * per_candidate_unit`. If that patch deployed, proxy might be reporting inflated units but quota service could still be using the old calculation, hence the dashboard (based on quota-service) shows low usage while proxy blocks the request.

dave_sre: confirm: which side actually enforces limits? If the proxy enforces locally we can see 429s even if central quota hasn't caught up.

carol_runtime: currently both exist: we have a fast-path local token bucket for global SLOs (edge-proxy) and a central quota-service for billing/accounting. The fast-path was introduced to avoid latency spikes but it must use the same unit math. Looks like a drift.

alice_support: Ben, our initial mitigation while we investigate: reduce candidates per request (try 8-10) and add exponential backoff on 429s. Can you try? Also I created a temporary support override if we need to lift the proxy limiter for your account.

ben_acme: I can change client tomorrow morning — want to avoid breaking traffic overnight. Appreciate an override.

carol_runtime: I'll repro locally. Steps I'm running:```bash
# simulate rerank producer at 10 rps with 50 candidates
for i in $(seq 1 100); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/rerank -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACT' -d '{"query":"q","candidates":['$(printf '"a",%.0s' {1..50})']}' &
  sleep 0.1
done
```Capturing response headers and unit accounting at the proxy.

carol_runtime: repro successful. Proxy increments units by `candidates_count *  (per_candidate_unit=1) * weight` = 50 * 1 *  (we recently started weighting by model_cost_factor=~0.3 then rounding up) => 50 * 0.3 => was rounding to 15 but due to a bug the float multiply was done after rounding, resulting in 50 * 1 -> 50 * per-request multiplier  => 360 observed because additional multiplier applied for long candidates list. So proxy thinks request consumed 360 units. Quota-service still uses the old formula and recorded +1 per request.

dave_sre: root cause sounds like order-of-operations bug in PR #4237 (weighting applied twice / wrong rounding). Can we patch edge-proxy quickly to align math and deploy hotfix to edge only?

carol_runtime: yes. I'll open a hotfix PR that changes unit calc to:```go
// pseudocode
units := int(math.Ceil(float64(candidatesCount) * per_candidate_unit * model_cost_factor))
// ensure we do multiplication before rounding and only once
```Deploy to canary edge nodes first.

alice_support: action items for support: 1) if Ben wants, apply temporary override to bypass proxy limiter for account=acme (will be a short-lived flag) 2) offer to batch fewer candidates as workaround 3) if they got charged unusually, open billing review. Ben, want me to enable override now?

ben_acme: Yes please enable override for the next 4 hours and we'll schedule client changes tomorrow morning. Also please let us know when fixed so we can revert the override.

dave_sre: override applied: feature-flag `bypass_rerank_edge_rl_acme=true` until 1802606721. Noted. Also created alert to revoke if abnormal traffic detected.

carol_runtime: hotfix PR open: #4279. I patched calc and added unit tests. Rolling to canary (2 nodes) now. Canary logs show units_reported now match quota-service increments for identical requests.

ops-bot: Deploy notification: canary-deploy pr/4279 -> edge-canary cluster started at 1802604700. 2/2 nodes healthy.

carol_runtime: After canary looked good for 10m I rolled to 60% of edge. Observed 429s drop to zero for the repro load. Scheduling full rollout in 15m.

alice_support: Ben — hotfix is in progress and we applied a temporary bypass for your account. You should be unblocked now. Can you confirm no more 429s?

ben_acme: Confirmed — traffic solid for the last 10 min, no 429s. Thanks!

carol_runtime: Postmortem notes: root cause = unit calculation regression from PR #4237 (edge-proxy multiplicative ordering bug). Fix = PR #4279 aligns proxy math with quota-service and adds regression tests for candidate-heavy requests. Follow-ups: add e2e test that runs a few high-candidate flows against both proxy and quota-service and assert unit parity; add tracing to surface unit calc per-request in dashboards; schedule audit for other endpoints that had similar weighting changes.

dave_sre: Also: we should move to central enforcement by default and use proxy fast-path only as a leaky bucket that consults central policy periodically to avoid dual-source drift. Filed infra ticket INF-886.

alice_support: Customer update will include: apology, summary of root cause, mitigations (override + hotfix), and next steps (billing review if any unexpected charges). I'll send draft to Carol for technical accuracy.

carol_runtime: I'll review. Thanks everyone. 

alice_support: Closing thread once Ben confirms no further issues. :white_check_mark:
